correctness.rationale: Lucas digit factorization and the published exact 2M_n identity yield the displayed three-case quotient rule with valid modular inverses. The trailing-maximal-digit recursion partitions every integer, gives normalized geometric cylinder mass and O_p(log N) counting discrepancy. For p=13 the first thirteen digit values, eleven fixed outputs and two explicit boundary maps give the exhaustive support and the all-k histogram, with the all-twelve boundary term counted exactly. The supplied standalone checker independently tested integer recurrences for 2501 indices, all applicable sampled primes and full p=13 blocks through 13^4. No finite sample is substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Kohen 2024 states a zero-density problem and a digit symmetry, with a separate formula expressing Motzkin terms through adjacent central-trinomial terms. Prior work gives Lucas digits, individual zero distributions, and modulo-five pair laws; these strong antecedents are explicitly used. However the conditional all-prime normalized ratio support and rational frequencies, the all-index forbidden ratio 11 at prime 13, and the full thirteen-power quotient histogram were not stated or established in the primary statements inspected. The calculation requires a complete geometric distribution of maximal-digit carry ratios and its affine pushforward. Possible implicit derivability from prior automata machinery is named as a priority risk.
residual_risks: The finite-state approach may allow an implicit or unindexed earlier normalized quotient theorem; the search cannot prove absence of all prior equivalents.
Available older ledgers beyond the accessible current-week file were not recovered; historical overlap exclusion is limited accordingly.
Some reviewed primary papers were inspected through available relevant statements and page images rather than every page.

value.rationale: The quotient is a canonical, unit-normalized arithmetic comparison of two linked classical combinatorial sequences, avoiding arbitrary parameter slicing. The full image and rational density law for every zero-free prime is an exact natural invariant. The p=13 case yields the substantive all-index forbidden linear congruence M_n!=11T_n mod13, proves every other ratio is attained infinitely often, and gives a 13-entry exact block census with strong nonuniformity, which the individual zero-density and p=5 pair results do not provide.
